title: bmonitor · Blackmagic Camera monitor and remote control for Mac
description: Monitor and remote-control the Blackmagic Camera app on your iPhone from your Mac. Free, open-source Mac app: live video and sound over Wi‑Fi, about 0.3 s behind, plus record, ISO, shutter, white balance and focus.
hero_sub: The free Mac app that monitors and remote-controls the Blackmagic Camera app on your iPhone. See the shot, hear the mic and start recording from your desk, over Wi‑Fi, about 0.3 s behind.
hero_meta: Free and open source · macOS 14 or later · Apple Silicon and Intel · Public beta

features_title:
Readable from across the room.
Built to feel native.
feat_1_body: Recording, timecode, the active mic and the minutes left on the iPhone stay large in the top corners. A red border tells you you're rolling.
feat_2_body: Click anywhere on the video and the iPhone focuses there. Zoom, lens and stabilization are one click away too.
feat_3_body: ISO, shutter (speed or angle), white balance with light presets and tint. The Mac shows the value the camera confirmed, not the one you asked for.
feat_4_body: The mic's name and an L/R meter in Blackmagic's own green, yellow and red. The camera's sound can play on the Mac, muted by default.
feat_5_body: I for ISO, S for shutter, W for white balance, ⌘R to record. Press ⌘/ to see them all.
setup_title:
Set it up once.
Then just open it.
setup_sub: After the first time, bmonitor finds the iPhone by itself.
step_1_body: Open the .dmg and drag bmonitor to Applications.
step_2_body: When the Mac asks to let bmonitor find devices on your local network, click Allow.
step_3_body: In its settings, set Remote Camera Control to Remote Camera and turn on the HTTP server.
step_4_body: Same Wi‑Fi, Blackmagic Camera on the camera screen, auto-lock off. Open bmonitor.
a1: A Mac with macOS 14 Sonoma or later (Apple Silicon or Intel), an iPhone with the free Blackmagic Camera app, and both on the same Wi‑Fi network.
q2: Does it record on my Mac?
a2: No. Recording stays on the iPhone, in the quality you chose there. The Mac is the monitor and the remote control.
q3: How far behind real time is the video?
a3: About 0.3 s glass to glass, most of it on the iPhone side. Enough to check framing, focus and sound while you talk.
q4: What does it change on my iPhone?
a4: It adds a streaming platform called “Mac Monitor SRT” to Blackmagic Camera and makes it active while bmonitor is open. When you quit, it stops the stream and restores the platform you had before.
q5: Can I use more than one iPhone?
a5: One at a time. If there's more than one on the network, bmonitor asks which one to use.
a6: It's a public beta. It works every day on the author's setup, but it was tested on one Mac and one iPhone, so expect rough edges and report what you find.
q7: Is it made by Blackmagic Design?
a7: No. bmonitor is an independent project that talks to Blackmagic Camera through its documented remote API and live stream.
a8: Yes. Free and open source (MIT), with no ads, no account and no paid version. It collects nothing and only talks to the iPhone on your network. If it's useful to you, a coffee is welcome and never required.

q9: Is there a Blackmagic Camera app for Mac?
a9: Blackmagic Camera is built for iPhone, iPad and Android. To watch and control it from a Mac you need a separate app, and that's what bmonitor is: the Mac side of Blackmagic Camera, free and open source.
q10: How do I control my iPhone camera from my Mac?
a10: Record with the Blackmagic Camera app on the iPhone and open bmonitor on the Mac. You get the live picture and sound, and you can start recording and change ISO, shutter, white balance, focus, zoom and lens from the Mac. Continuity Camera is different: it turns the iPhone into a webcam for Mac apps and doesn't control a recording on the iPhone.
q11: How is this different from Blackmagic's own remote monitoring?
a11: Blackmagic Camera can be monitored and controlled from a second iPhone or iPad running Blackmagic Camera, or from its Apple Watch companion. bmonitor does it from your Mac instead, in a regular window you can keep beside your script.
